description.narrative: (Uganda): LPHS Eastern was awarded to a local organization and will support TB and HIV interventions in 15 districts in the Eastern region of Uganda. With FY 2022 TB funds, the activity will prioritize the following areas: 1) screening and detection of all forms of TB in infants, children, and adults at facility and community levels; 2) early initiation and completion of anti-TB treatment for all patients diagnosed with all forms of TB; 3) ensuring strong community systems to strengthen the continuum of TB prevention, screening, diagnosis, care, and treatment; and 4) improving the quality of the multi-drug resistant TB program and TB/HIV collaborative activities through the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment cascade.The priority interventions will include: 1) strengthening community TB case finding through community sensitization and engagement; 2) improving linkages between communities and health facilities; 3) scaling up contact tracing approaches; and 4) addressing socio-cultural barriers to accessing TB treatment and prevention services.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, the activity will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment to protect service providers and beneficiaries of TB services. LPHS Eastern will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services. By working closely with community partners including Village Health Teams (VHT) in increasing health seeking behavior, the activity will mitigate service disruption as a result of climatic conditions.Health systems strengthening activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level...
